source.title: Blurs Behave Like Ensembles: Spatial Smoothings to Improve Accuracy, Uncertainty, and Robustness

record.file_problem: Full text is present; no truncation or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training and test performance comparisons for classifier heads and analyzes loss landscapes, but does not test the specific claim versions about random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness tracking the train-test gap, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The classifier-head comparison reports training and test NLL and errors, but does not compare train-test gaps for any listed version. Hessian and loss-landscape results do not test whether the magnitude-aware sharpness measure tracks generalization gaps.
record.test_reason: The record overlooks V6: Table E.1 and Table C.2 compare held-out accuracy with and without MC dropout, Figure A.1 varies dropout rate, and Appendix C.1 reports removing dropout from MLP classifier heads. These are tests of dropout's effect on generalization, although MC-dropout inference also averages stochastic predictions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors argue that spatial smoothing improves accuracy, uncertainty estimation, and robustness by aggregating feature maps and stabilizing optimization. They argue that parameter-count-based overfitting prevention is insufficient to explain GAP's advantage over MLP heads. This is their interpretation, rather than proof that MLP heads never overfit.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies spatial smoothing and classifier-head comparisons, rather than the interventions and measurements in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the predictive-performance improvement from spatial smoothing decreases with network depth, is relatively marginal for ResNeXt, and depends on blur-kernel shape; classifier-head results vary by model.

fits_no_version.finding: GAP generally improves test performance relative to MLP heads on otherwise convolutional networks. ResNet-18 is an exception to the authors' broad training-performance interpretation: its MLP head has lower training NLL than GAP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pooling-based CNN classifier heads can improve held-out performance relative to MLP heads; fewer parameters alone do not explain the observed differences.

fits_no_version.finding: Spatial smoothing and GAP suppress Hessian eigenvalue outliers and stabilize loss landscapes. These measurements do not establish magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spatial averaging can smooth stochastic CNN training objectives and improve predictive performance.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: The relevant classifier-head comparison is limited to CIFAR-100 and MC-dropout models. The paper reports averages of three evaluations; it says standard deviations are significantly smaller than the improvements, but omits standard deviations from tables. Its Hessian max-eigenvalue spectrum is an analysis of loss-landscape smoothness, not a test of the version’s magnitude-aware sharpness/generalization-gap relation.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the classifier-head performance results do not measure any listed version, and the Hessian/loss-landscape measurements do not measure the train-test gap named by V7.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch; changing a CNN classifier head does not test this comparison.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.

Very small training sets, removing dropout and weight decay together, and whether excessive dropout causes training underfit. MC-dropout comparisons do not isolate training regularization from stochastic inference averaging.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.

missing.what: Held-out accuracy comparisons between deterministic and MC-dropout classifiers, separately for every architecture, dataset, and spatial-smoothing condition. Record inference ensemble size, dropout rate, and the shared weight-decay and augmentation recipe.
missing.locator: Table E.1; Appendix A.1; Figure E.1

missing.what: Dropout versus no-dropout accuracy comparisons under both post-activation and pre-activation arrangements, including the substantial VGG-19 pre-activation improvement and the mixed results elsewhere.

Accuracy dependence on dropout rate, separately by spatial smoothing and inference ensemble size. Exact plotted values are not reliably recoverable from the supplied text, but the direction is stated explicitly.
missing.locator: Figure A.1 and caption; Appendix A.1

missing.what: The qualitative result that removing 50% dropout from MLP classifier heads severely degrades ResNet test performance; numerical values are not supplied.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set and declaration that no results map to any version are incorrect for V6. Verdicts use the supplied text pending extraction of the missing comparisons. MC dropout uses 50 inference samples by default, so its comparison with deterministic networks combines dropout training with prediction averaging. Improved NLL or calibration alone is not treated as reduced classification error.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch; the paper compares classifier heads on CNNs.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch training and adaptation of training recipes.
The stated dropout comparisons across training-set regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations and their relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

relationships.reason: Table C.2 increases test accuracy from 64.4% without dropout to 70.1% with dropout; this supporting comparison is missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Higher test accuracy was reported for combined dropout training and stochastic inference, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Unsmoothened VGG and ResNet classifiers on CIFAR and ImageNet.
relationships.reason: Table E.1 shows lower accuracy with MC dropout for VGG-19/CIFAR-10 (93.1% to 92.6%), VGG-16/CIFAR-100 (71.6% to 68.8%), VGG-19/CIFAR-100 (67.6% to 67.3%), ResNet-18/CIFAR-100 (77.9% to 77.3%), ResNet-50/CIFAR-100 (79.9% to 79.1%), and ResNet-18/ImageNet (70.3% to 70.0%); these comparisons are missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Monte Carlo (MC) dropout reportedly lowered accuracy across the listed classifiers. These comparisons have not been independently checked and combined dropout during training with predictions that vary randomly.
